learning_resources.title: Malware Analysis - Unpacking NetWiredRC With DnSpy
learning_resources.creator: MalwareAnalysisForHedgehogs
learning_resources.skills: Trace a managed decrypt-to-Assembly.Load path; break after decryption, inspect Locals, show byte array in memory and save selected payload without executing the recovered stage.
learning_resources.prerequisites: Supplied/pre-extracted managed stage, C# reading, basic dnSpyEx navigation, prepared isolated lab if practicing.
learning_resources.limitations: Only 13:00–16:30 is assigned. Start from a supplied or already-extracted .NET stage in a prepared isolated lab. Earlier PEStudio/PortEx/Visual Studio and later de4dot workflows are excluded, not event-approved dependencies. Historical dnSpy UI; verify dnSpyEx equivalents. No claim that this handles every .NET packer or supplies a complete standalone extraction lab.

access.cost: Free streaming; no new account used for metadata/captions.
access.offline: Video download rights not established. Free text alternative covers loaded-module inspection, not identical byte-array dumping.

evidence.inspected: Read local automatic captions for 13:00–16:30. 13:07–14:37 traces bytes through splitting/decrypt/Assembly.Load; 15:02–15:30 places breakpoint after decode; 15:34–16:00 inspects Locals and MZ-like prefix; 16:04–16:23 Show in Memory and save selected bytes; 16:23 explicitly stops instead of running recovered stage. Automatic captions misrecognize dnSpy and hex values; MZ alone is a lead, validate PE headers afterwards.

learning_resources.practice: On a benign pre-existing managed loader, predict the point at which decoded bytes become available. Pause before loading the payload, inspect array length/header, and explain why successful byte dumping does not prove a valid or safe executable.
